title: Embed/Rerank compatibility playbook: unified error taxonomy, streaming cursor semantics, and client adapter guidance
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: produce a prescriptive playbook and SDK adapter spec that ensures parity between legacy embeddings/rerank endpoints and the unified vector API for: 1) error code mapping and retry semantics, 2) pagination/iterator behavior for streaming and non-streaming flows, and 3) structured output expectations when tool/function-calling is layered on top. The playbook will include canonical error taxonomy, backward-compatible HTTP status -> structured error mapping, cursor lifecycle rules (checkpointing, tombstones, resume behavior), and recommended adapter strategies for server-side proxies and client SDKs. Background: several customers reported client breakages after migration to the unified vector endpoint when mixing streaming rerank with legacy cursor-based pagination. Engineering has implemented multiple fixes (ENG-48210, ENG-59382). This ticket synthesizes those learnings into a single migration/playbook artifact and produces test vectors and SDK change proposals.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Canonical error mapping doc published (HTTP status -> machine-friendly error_code -> retry_hint) and agreed by API/SDK/eng
A2: Cursor semantics defined for streaming iterators: checkpoint format, resume token invariants, and tombstone rules; spec includes examples for partial responses and deduplication
A3: SDK adapter reference implementation (node+python) demonstrating graceful fallback from streaming to paginated mode and mapping legacy client expectations
A4: Backcompat test suite with representative fixtures added to ember-compat-tests and passing in CI
A5: Migration guide published with roll-forward/rollback playbook and customer-facing FAQ
risks_and_open_questions: RQ1: Client libraries with custom retry logic may interpret new retry_hint semantics incorrectly — do we need opt-in headers?
RQ2: Some legacy clients depend on numeric-only cursor tokens (no metadata) — how to encode tombstone hints without breaking those clients?
RQ3: Interaction between function/tool-calls that emit structured outputs and streaming partial rerank scores — how to preserve deterministic ordering and idempotency?
initial_proposal: 1) Publish an error taxonomy that maps all historical HTTP statuses used by embeddings/rerank flows to a small set of machine error_codes (e.g., RATE_LIMIT, BACKEND_OVERLOAD, INVALID_CURSOR, STALE_RESULT, UNEXPECTED_FORMAT). Each mapping includes a retry_hint (immediate, backoff, no-retry) and human_message. 2) Define a stable cursor envelope: base64(JSON) that includes: cursor_id, seq, checksum, tombstone_flag optional, and server_hint. Legacy purely opaque numeric cursors remain supported via adapter wrapping. 3) Streaming iterator semantics: streaming responses emit a sequence of objects with guaranteed per-item sequence numbers. Resume tokens point to last emitted seq. On resume, server will re-emit up to N items prior to the resume seq for safe dedupe. 4) SDK adapter patterns: server-side proxy option (translate legacy requests -> unified API) and client-side shim (thin adapter in SDKs) with explicit compatibility headers: X-Redwood-Compat: embed-rerank-v1 and X-Redwood-Resume-Mode: dedupe|strict. 5) Structured outputs: when tool-calls are used inside rerank pipelines, schema versioning must be included in the cursor envelope and in the streaming item metadata to ensure clients can validate partial structured objects.
workplan: Week 1: Draft error taxonomy and cursor envelope spec; sync with runtime/serving and SDK leads
Week 2: Build adapter reference (node) + unit tests; add fixtures for streaming resume/dedupe cases
Week 3: Publish migration guide and run internal compatibility job across customer-mirroring tenants
Week 4: Iterate on feedback, update SDKs (python/node), and cut documentation PR
implementation_notes: Note: runtime must support 'replay window' configurable per-model to bound how many items are re-emitted during resume to simplify dedupe logic
Prefer explicit schema_version in streaming records to allow clients to perform forward/backward compatibility checks
Avoid changing existing HTTP status codes for general errors; implement mapping in gateway to preserve legacy surface while exposing machine error codes in response body
Consider opt-in compatibility header for high-risk customers to enable feature-flagged rollout
